messages.text: When does the lunar eclipse begin?

A total lunar eclipse will be visible in Glendale, Arizona, on the night of March 13, 2025. The eclipse will begin with the penumbral phase at 8:57 PM MST, followed by the partial phase at 10:09 PM MST. Totality, when the Earth's shadow completely covers the Moon, will start at 11:26 PM MST and last until 12:31 AM MST on March 14. The partial phase will end at 1:47 AM MST, and the penumbral phase will conclude at 3:00 AM MST. citeturn0search1

During totality, the Moon will appear reddish due to Earth's atmosphere filtering out shorter-wavelength blue light, a phenomenon often referred to as a "Blood Moon." citeturn0search3

For an enhanced viewing experience, Glendale Community College's North Campus Observatory is hosting a free public event from 8:00 PM to midnight on March 13. The umbral stages to full eclipse will be observable from 8:50 PM to midnight. citeturn0search4

No special equipment is needed to observe the eclipse, but binoculars or a telescope can provide a more detailed view. citeturn0news9
